The Court made the following Judgment:
Challenge in this Motor Accidents Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is to the Award, dated 15.02.2016, in M.V.O.P. No.813 of 2007 on the file of Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge, West Godavari, Eluru (for short,
'the Tribunal') whereunder the Tribunal dealing with the claim of compensation sought by the claimants to a tune of Rs.9,00,000/- for the death of Janyavula Rambabu (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased') in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 25.09.2006 at about 03:30 PM, awarded a sum of Rs.6,01,000/- towards compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge, West Godavari, Eluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties to this Appeal will hereinafter be referred to as described before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.

3. The case of the claimants, in brief, according to the averments set out in the claim, before the Tribunal, is that first petitioner is the wife, second and third petitioners are the parents and fourth petitioner is the minor daughter of the deceased.

On 25.09.2006 the deceased and one P. Srinivasa Rao were AVRB,J proceeding on Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle bearing No.AP 37 AA 3663 driven by the deceased cautiously and when they reached palm oil factory at about 03:30 p.m. the first respondent being the driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing Nos.AP 37 AP 297 and AP 37 U 4033 (for short, 'the offending vehicle') drove the same in a rash and negligent manner at high speed without blowing horn, without following traffic rules and dashed against the motorcycle.
As a result the deceased succumbed to injuries on the spot.
The pillion rider received multiple grievous injuries.
Due to the rash and negligent driving of the first respondent, the accident was occurred.
Station House Officer, Pedavegi Police Station registered a case in Crime No.141 of 2006 against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sections 304-A and 337 IPC.
First respondent is the driver and second respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Third respondent is the insurer of the Trailer bearing No.AP 37 U 4033 and fourth respondent is the insurer of the Tractor bearing No.AP 37 AP 297 respectively.

Fifth respondent is the legal representative of second respondent,
owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

4. First respondent, driver of the offending vehicle, adopted the counter filed by the fifth respondent.
5. Second respondent died during pendency of the Petition.

6. Third respondent, insurer of the trailer, filed counter denying allegations of the petitioners contending in substance that the AVRB,J deceased drove the motorcycle and crossed an Auto which was suddenly stopped in front of the motorcycle and in that process, he drove the motorcycle against the tractor coming in the opposite direction and the tractor dashed the motorcycle of the deceased.
The deceased was negligent as he went to right side by crossing the auto.
There is no rash and negligence on the part of the first respondent, driver of the offending vehicle, and there was fault on the part of the deceased.

7. The fourth respondent filed its counter denying the averments of the petitioners more particularly contending that the accident occurred was due to rash and negligent driving of the first respondent but not the deceased and the fourth respondent was un- necessarily added to the proceedings as such it is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation and rate of interest are excessive.

8. The fifth respondent filed her counter denying all the averments in the petition contending in substance that the alleged accident occurred was due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased,
who drove the motorcycle carelessly and rashly without observing the traffic, took turn negligently and dashed against the vehicle of the first respondent and caused the accident.
The owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.AP 37 AA 3663 are also necessary parties to the proceedings.
The petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties.
The fifth respondent was holding all vehicular documents as such they are in force at the time of accident.
As the insurance policy is in force, the third respondent is AVRB,J liable to pay compensation, if any, to the petitioners under the contract of indemnity.
The petitioners have to prove the age, income, manner of the accident and the rash and negligent driving of the first respondent and prayed to dismiss the petition against the fifth respondent.

9. The Tribunal, on the basis of the aforesaid pleadings, settled the following issues for trial:
1.

Whether the deceased-Janyavula Rambabu died in a motor vehicle accident on 25.09.2006, due to rash and negligent driving of Tractor and Trailer bearing No.AP 37 AP 297 and AP 37 U 4033 driven by first respondent?
2. What was the age and income of the deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from which of the respondents?
3.
To what relief?

sentences.text: During the course of trial on behalf of the petitioners before the Tribunal, PWs.1 to PW.4 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-5 were marked.
On behalf of the contesting respondents, RWs.1 and RW.2 were examined and Exs.B-1 to B-4 were marked.

11. The Tribunal, on hearing both sides and after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, answered the issues in favour of the claimants and against the respondents and awarded a sum of Rs.6,01,000/- and apportioned Rs.3,01,000/- to the first AVRB,J petitioner/wife and Rs.1,00,000/- each to the second, third and fourth petitioners respectively.
12. The appellants/claimants, feeling that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is not just and reasonable, filed the present Appeal with a prayer to enhance the compensation.

13. As against the findings of the Tribunal that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving made by the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., by the first respondent, there is no cross- objection or cross-appeal filed by the respondents.
So, the scope of the present Appeal is very limited.

14. Now in deciding the present Appeal, the simple question that falls for consideration is:
Whether the Award of the Tribunal, dated 15.02.2016, in M.V.O.P. No.813 of 2007,
on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge, West Godavari, Eluru is sustainable under law and facts and whether there are any grounds to interfere with the same?

sentences.text: Sri B.V. Krishna Reddy, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants, would canvass a contention that, in fact, the claimants are entitled for more compensation than claimed.

To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners examined PW.3 - AVRB,J Yerra Yesu Babu, B-Grade License Electrical Contractor, who testified that the deceased used to work with him and he used to pay a salary of Rs.14,000/- p.m. to the deceased and as such he issued Ex.A-5 - salary certificate.
PW.3 who issued Ex.A-5 stepped into the witness box to speak of the salary but the Tribunal erroneously disbelieved his evidence.
His evidence remained un- shaked during the cross-examination.

He would further contend that if the income of Rs.14,000/-
p.m. is considered, the loss of dependency would be Rs.22,68,000/-.
He would further submit that even there is no bar to award compensation of Rs.22,68,000/-.

In support of his contentions, he would rely upon the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Shiv Kumar and others v. Gainda Lal and others1, Saroj Devi and others v. The New India Assurance Company Limited2, a decision of the Rajasthan High Court in Asha and others v. Naresh Kumar and others3 and a decision of the Madras High Court in Sagunthala and others v. Bakkiyam and others4 16.

sentences.text: Smt. P. Satya Manjula, learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer, would canvass a contention that the Tribunal did not fix up any responsibility against the third respondent and the Tribunal fixed up the responsibility against the owner, driver and insurer of the offending vehicle only.

18. No arguments are advanced on behalf of first and fifth respondents.
19.
As seen from the evidence of PW.1, who is the wife of deceased, she put forth the facts in tune with her pleadings and through her examination, Exs.A-1 to A-5 were marked.
Petitioners examined PW.2, direct witness to the occurrence, to prove the rash and negligent act alleged against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Claimants examined PW.3, to speak of the so called salary which he used to pay to the deceased under the cover of Ex.A-5.
20.
The crucial question that has to be considered here is as to what was the income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The contention of the claimants is that the deceased was an electrician and he was getting a sum of Rs.9,000/- p.m.
It is no doubt true that contrary to the pleadings, they brought into picture Ex.A-5 through examination of PW.3.
The Tribunal disbelieved the theory of PW.3.
The contention of the appellants is that the evidence of PW.3 remained un-shaked.
As seen from the evidence of PW.3, during the course of cross-examination, he deposed certain answers which shattered his evidence to any extent.
PW.3 is said to be a private contractor under whom deceased used to work.
AVRB,J
In cross-examination, he deposed that since 1995, he was in contract works.
Contract license is required to be renewed for every two years.
He could not say how many workers were being engaged by him since 1995.
He did not inform to the Labour Officer about the number of workers working under him.
He did not file any piece of record as to how many workers worked under him.
He did not place any material to show that he paid wages to the workers.
So, all this goes to show that he had no piece of material except the so called Ex.A-5 to say that he used to pay wages to the workers.
The evidence of PW.3 cannot stand to the test of scrutiny.
The contention of the appellants that the evidence of PW.3 remain un- impeached is devoid of merits.
So, the accident was occurred in the year 2006.
The minimum wages which a person was supposed to get as on that date was around Rs.3,000/- p.m.

Hence, the Tribunal rightly considered his notional annual income as that of Rs.36,000/- and deducted 1/4th of the same towards his personal and living expenses of the deceased and arrived at the net annual income of Rs.27,000/- towards his family members.

Adverting to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Road Transport Corporation and another5, the Tribunal applied the multiplier 18 as the deceased was aged about 23 years.

sentences.text: So, the act of the Tribunal in arriving at the multiplicand as Rs.4,86,000/- is reasonable.
Under the conventional heads, the Tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.50,000/- towards consortium.

According to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance AIR (2009) SC 3104 Janyavula Kanaka Durga 3 Others vs Tata Rambabu 4 Others on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152853759/
5 AVRB,J Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others6, the amount of compensation to be awarded under conventional heads is only Rs.70,000/-.

sentences.text:
Apart from this by considering the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others7, the children are entitled to parental consortium, as such the fourth petitioner,
who is the daughter of the deceased is entitled to loss of parental consortium to a tune of Rs.40,000/-.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the total amount to be awarded under the conventional heads is Rs.1,10,000/-.
The amount of Rs.1,10,000/- under the conventional heads if is added to the Rs.4,86,000/-, it would work out to Rs.5,96,000/-.
However, the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal is Rs.6,01,000/-.
This is the claimants appeal.

In the absence of any cross-objection or cross-appeal,
the compensation awarded by the Tribunal cannot be reduced.
21. This Court has looked into the decisions cited by learned counsel for the appellants.
Dealing with the facts and circumstances therein, the Hon'ble Apex Court, Rajasthan High Court and the Madras High Court dealt with the claims therein.

22. Insofar as the legal principles are concerned, the Tribunal rightly applied the multiplier 18 considering the age of the deceased as 23 years and the compensation under the conventional heads awarded is also almost in accordance with law.
The notional income of the deceased is to be arrived at by looking into the prevailing 2017 (16) SCC 680 2018 (18) SCC 130 AVRB,J wages which were in force as on the date of accident.
In the absence of any definite proof as regards the income, the evidence of PW.3 coupled with Ex.A-5 is not at all believable.
Under the circumstances, this Court does not see any reason to interfere with the well reasoned award of the Tribunal.

23. In the result, the Motor Accidents Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed confirming the award,
dated 15.02.2016, in M.V.O.P. No.813 of 2007 on the file of Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge, West Godavari, Eluru.
